name: contract-method-state-counts
goal: Reject duplicate method-state cases and retain existing supported case identities when other capabilities expand

evidence: A new lifecycle proposal exposes two cases for the same scanned/initialized slot. The validator accepts at-least-one rather than exactly-one; the count guard also lets an unrelated new state excuse another old-state case or rename. Those loopholes permit standalone bug tests despite declared counts.

Strengthen the existing validator method case and existing compare method case for duplicate slots, unknown methods, unused new states and preserved old identities. Keep one validator case and two TestContractService cases; no new test declarations.

Atcee40ae6d0 the unchanged one-case validator suite accepts a duplicate Runner.run/ready case, and the unchanged compare case accepts old-state inflation after adding an unused new state. Retained red checkpoint names the exactly-one-method/state assertion; three total owning tests remain fixed.

Every method/state permits exactly one case, orphan subjects are rejected, retained capabilities preserve their IDs and titles, and a new case must reference its actual added state, method, example, prop or error. Seven focused tests passed before the explicit in-memory admission characterization was added; source lint and registry checks pass. The final characterized green proof remains pending resource headroom.
